report.source_text: On systemic and neurological examinations, the patient had a GCS of 15/15, oriented to time, people, and place, with normal speech and good long- and short-term memory. Cranial nerves (1-XII) were all intact, and no signs and symptoms of meningeal irritation, with normal tone and reflexes with power of 5/5 on both lower and upper limbs; superficial and deep tendon reflexes were normal, sensory system intact with normal coordination, gait and balance.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old male with a four-year history of progressive itchy rash initially macules and papules on trunk, limbs, and face, which ulcerated and were refractory to eczema treatments. Examination showed multiple erosive plaques, nodules, and tumors covering >95% body surface. Skin biopsy revealed histopathological features consistent with Mycosis Fungoides with prominent spongiosis and CD3 positivity on immunohistochemistry. Systemic workup including HIV serology, chest X-ray, and abdominal ultrasound was normal. The patient denied constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats. Neurological and systemic exams were normal. Based on clinical, histological, and immunophenotypic findings, and ISCL scoring (6 points), a diagnosis of MF was established.
